case: A 59-year-old man with a history of obesity, dyslipidemia, and hypertension was evaluated for hepatocellular carcinoma. Twelve years earlier, elevated aminotransferases led to a presumptive diagnosis of metabolic dysfunction–associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Liver biopsy 9 years prior showed macrovesicular steatosis, hepatocyte ballooning, and bridging fibrosis (stage 3), confirming metabolic dysfunction–associated steatohepatitis (MASH). Imaging revealed cirrhosis with splenomegaly and varices. Surveillance imaging detected a liver lesion that enlarged over time, eventually leading to a diagnosis of hepatocellular carcinoma. The patient underwent multiple locoregional therapies (alcohol ablation, radiofrequency ablation) while awaiting transplant. Nineteen months later, he received a liver transplant. Pathology of the explanted liver confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma with vascular invasion. Post-transplant follow-up revealed good clinical outcomes, though the patient developed cardiometabolic complications including dyslipidemia, post-transplant diabetes, and atrial arrhythmia requiring pacemaker implantation.

A 63-year-old woman presented with a 2-month history of progressive dyspnea on exertion, fatigue, abdominal distention, anorexia, dry cough, and edema. She had a history of rheumatoid arthritis diagnosed 15 months earlier, treated with methotrexate, which was later discontinued. Her past medical history included diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, a resected meningioma, and H. pylori gastritis. Imaging revealed pericardial and pleural effusions, soft-tissue thickening around the aorta, perirenal fibrosis, and mediastinal involvement. She also reported polyuria and polydipsia, and was diagnosed with central diabetes insipidus. PET-CT showed FDG uptake in bones and retroperitoneal tissue. Biopsy revealed foamy histiocytes positive for CD68, CD163, and BRAF V600E mutation. Diagnosis of Erdheim–Chester disease was confirmed. Due to QTc prolongation, treatment with vemurafenib was avoided, and cobimetinib (a MEK inhibitor) was initiated, with clinical and radiologic improvement.
